rationale: The candidate is a coherent stepped mass in all four views, so it is not failing on legibility or multi-view consistency. It does, however, read primarily as a generic stepped/terraced block rather than a clearly programmed neighborhood-living mass with an active street threshold. The blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly: the form does not carve a convincing public void, seam, or grounded entry condition toward that edge, and the section feels more like stacked setback volumes than an occupiable street-building relationship. The silhouette is clear but too stair-like and not yet capacity-bearing or program-specific enough to earn a high section/program fit. Parcel response appears generally contained and oriented, but the dominant gesture does not yet exploit the parcel/access logic into a legible public ground figure. The form has repairable integrity; it is not visibly self-colliding across views, but it needs a stronger carve or threshold and a less repetitive step mass to better match the brief.
